attribution.note: Marcus states the forecast in his own voice.

semantics.note: The firm prediction concerns general use of private data. No deadline or conditional antecedent is stated. Lack of affirmative permission is a reasonable reading of the qualifier.

contract.note: Default use of nonpublic information is a fair ordinary reading. The contract appropriately distinguishes this from ignoring exercised opt-outs or inevitably using every individual's data.

evidence.note: Google's dated disclosure establishes use of nonpublic chats in model improvement. This is company-reported practice, not an independent inspection of training data.
The dated independent policy study identifies Google's default training on chat inputs and an opt-out. It corroborates disclosed practices without inspecting underlying datasets.
Opt-outs, temporary chats and separate recording controls limit the claim's breadth. They do not contradict default participation for other nonpublic chat information.

reviews.rationale: Together, the post-publication disclosures and policy study establish nonpublic chat use for model improvement under default participation before the cutoff, satisfying the early-resolution rule. Available exclusions do not undo that occurrence or establish that explicit objections were ignored.
